description: We are a team of three student innovators passionate about technology, AI, sustainability and solving real-world problems. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we are building CropWise AI, a platform that uses NASA Earth observation data to support smarter, climate-resilient crop rotation decisions. We value creativity, collaboration and learning. We welcome teammates with skills in Python, data science, GIS, agriculture, APIs or AI/ML who want to make an impact!
summary:
CropWise AI – Climate-Informed Agricultural Decision Support

CropWise AI is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers navigate climate uncertainty and explore more informed crop rotation choices.

Using real historical and recent climate observations from NASA POWER, CropWise AI transforms complex environmental data into accessible, district-level insights, including rainfall variations, temperature anomalies, prolonged dry spells, and heat-related indicators.

The platform currently covers four agricultural districts in India: Ludhiana, Samastipur, Akola, and Thanjavur. Farmers can explore seasonal climate conditions, enter their farm details, and compare alternative crop rotation sequences through an interactive dashboard.

What makes CropWise AI distinctive is its commitment to transparent, evidence-aware decision support. Rather than presenting uncertain results as definitive recommendations, it clearly identifies illustrative comparison scores, confidence levels, missing information, and areas requiring expert validation.

By bridging NASA Earth observation data and agricultural planning, CropWise AI demonstrates how accessible climate intelligence can support climate awareness, encourage more resilient farming practices, and contribute to a more sustainable, food-secure future.
details:
CropWise AI – Project Details

1. Project Overview

CropWise AI is a climate-informed agricultural decision-support platform developed to bridge the gap between NASA Earth observation data and practical agricultural planning.

Farmers increasingly face unpredictable rainfall, rising temperatures, prolonged dry spells, and changing seasonal conditions. Although valuable environmental datasets are publicly available, interpreting them and connecting them to agricultural decisions can be challenging.

CropWise AI addresses this problem by transforming NASA POWER climate observations into understandable visual insights and illustrative crop rotation comparisons, helping users explore how local climate conditions may influence agricultural planning.

Our prototype currently supports four agricultural districts in India: Ludhiana (Punjab), Samastipur (Bihar), Akola (Maharashtra), and Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu).

2. How CropWise AI Works

Please review

The platform guides users through an interactive agricultural planning experience.

Step 1 – District Selection

Users select one of the four supported agricultural districts to explore location-specific climate conditions.

Step 2 – Farm Profile

Users provide basic agricultural information, including their current crop, water availability, soil type, farm size, and farming priorities. This creates context for exploring crop rotation alternatives.

Step 3 – NASA Climate Analysis

CropWise AI processes historical and recent observations from the NASA POWER Daily API to generate seasonal climate indicators, including:

  • Rainfall variation compared with historical conditions.
  • Temperature anomalies.
  • Consecutive dry-spell duration.
  • Heat-day indicators.

These indicators are displayed through a climate dashboard, allowing users to understand seasonal environmental patterns without interpreting raw climate datasets.

Step 4 – Crop Rotation Comparison

The platform presents three example crop rotation sequences for comparison. Available water-related and climate-resilience indicators are displayed alongside provisional comparison scores, supporting evidence, and explanations.

The scores are explicitly labelled as illustrative team estimates, not scientifically validated agricultural recommendations.

Step 5 – Transparent Decision Support

CropWise AI identifies missing assessment criteria, communicates uncertainty, and highlights where local agricultural expertise is necessary.

This helps users distinguish between observed environmental conditions and preliminary agricultural interpretations.

3. NASA Data and Technical Implementation

NASA Earth science data forms the foundation of CropWise AI.

We use the NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) Daily API to retrieve historical and recent environmental observations.

NASA POWER API:
https://power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/daily/point

The application uses four environmental parameters:

NASA Parameter

Purpose

T2M

Daily average air temperature

T2M_MAX

Daily maximum air temperature

PRECTOTCORR

Corrected daily precipitation

ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN

Surface solar radiation

The backend processes these observations into seasonal indicators that are accessible through REST APIs and displayed in the frontend.

The platform uses historical climate observations rather than claiming to predict future weather or crop yields. NASA provides the environmental data; our application performs the processing, visualization, and illustrative agricultural comparisons.

4. Tools and Technologies

CropWise AI was developed using a modern web application architecture.

Frontend Development

  • React and JavaScript for the interactive user interface.
  • Vite for frontend development and builds.
  • CSS and Tailwind CSS utilities for responsive styling.
  • Lucide React for interface icons.

Backend Development

  • Python for climate data processing and application logic.
  • FastAPI for backend REST API services.
  • JSON and Parquet files for processed datasets and application data.

Data Integration

  • NASA POWER Daily API for environmental observations.
  • Climate processing modules for seasonal analysis.
  • Rotation comparison logic for illustrative agricultural comparisons.

Development and Collaboration

  • Git and GitHub for version control and team collaboration.
  • API integration between the frontend climate dashboard, rotation comparison interface, and backend services.

The project is software-based and does not require specialized physical hardware.

5. What Makes CropWise AI Creative?

CropWise AI is designed around a simple idea: climate data becomes more valuable when people can understand its relevance to their decisions.

Our approach combines several elements:

Connecting Earth observations to agricultural choices

Instead of displaying climate statistics in isolation, CropWise AI places them alongside example crop rotation strategies, creating a more meaningful exploration experience.

District-specific climate intelligence

The prototype focuses on four geographically distinct Indian agricultural districts, demonstrating how environmental observations can be explored at a local scale.

Explainability over black-box recommendations

Rather than generating unexplained crop rankings, the platform communicates available evidence, confidence indicators, missing criteria, and limitations.

Responsible use of provisional data

Where scientifically validated agricultural information is unavailable, CropWise AI avoids presenting estimated values as established facts. This makes transparency an essential part of the product design.

Accessible and interactive experience

A guided workflow, visual dashboard, and English/Hindi interface help make complex environmental information easier to navigate.

6. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors when designing the platform.

Climate variability: Different agricultural regions experience different rainfall patterns, temperature conditions, and seasonal risks.

Data reliability: We distinguish NASA-derived observations from illustrative agricultural estimates and communicate data limitations.

Agricultural complexity: Crop rotation decisions depend on soil characteristics, irrigation availability, crop requirements, farming priorities, and local expertise—not climate data alone.

User accessibility: The interface prioritizes understandable explanations, visual indicators, and straightforward navigation.

Scientific responsibility: The platform avoids claiming that NASA directly recommends crops or that provisional scores are validated agronomic assessments.

Scalability: The modular frontend, backend, and climate-processing architecture provides a foundation for expanding district coverage and incorporating validated agricultural datasets.

7. Benefits and Intended Impact

CropWise AI aims to make climate information more accessible and useful for agricultural communities.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Climate awareness: Helping users better understand seasonal rainfall, temperature, and dry-spell patterns.
  • Informed exploration: Supporting comparison of alternative cropping sequences while acknowledging uncertainty.
  • Improved accessibility: Presenting NASA environmental data through an intuitive web interface.
  • Responsible decision support: Encouraging users to review evidence and seek expert guidance rather than relying on unverified recommendations.
  • Research opportunities: Establishing a foundation for collaboration with agricultural experts, researchers, and institutions.

In the longer term, the project could be expanded with validated crop suitability information, soil datasets, additional districts, and expert-reviewed agricultural models.

These improvements would require further research and validation before the platform could provide reliable farm-specific recommendations.

8. Our Vision

CropWise AI demonstrates how NASA's openly available environmental observations can be transformed into understandable, locally relevant agricultural insights.

Our goal is not to replace farmers' experience or agricultural experts, but to make climate information easier to access and interpret as part of informed agricultural planning.

By combining Earth observation data, accessible technology, and transparent decision support, we hope to contribute toward a future where more agricultural communities can better understand climate variability and explore resilient farming practices.

CropWise AI — Smarter Crop Rotations. Stronger Farms. A More Resilient India.
